entities.name: Acute lower-GI bleeding
observations: Ongoing significant hematochezia after resuscitation warrants prompt localization; CTA is a recommended initial imaging test.

entities.name: CT angiography
observations: CTA is used to localize active, hemodynamically significant lower-GI bleeding; positive localization can guide catheter angiography and embolization.

entities.name: Mesenteric angiography
observations: Catheter angiography can provide endovascular treatment after active bleeding is localized, commonly by CTA.

entities.name: PMID:25451447
observations: Cross-sectional survey of 3,667 adults in Tianjin, China; assessed soft-drink intake by food-frequency questionnaire and depressive symptoms with Zung SDS.

entities.name: Soft drinks-depression China adults
observations: Among 3,667 Tianjin adults, adjusted odds of elevated depressive symptoms (SDS≥50) across increasing soft-drink intake categories were 1.00, 1.43 (95% CI 1.01–2.01), and 2.00 (1.15–3.37); trend p<0.01.
Cross-sectional design cannot establish temporal direction or causation; similar associations were reported using SDS cutoffs of 40 or 45.
